- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects downward; add 1–3% buffer to prevent premature drop.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% for next period.
- Model shows strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment drops sharply, delay price correction by 1–3 days.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the forecast window; apply 1–3% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
